nesting.name: open_crates
nesting.prompt_body: A photorealistic warehouse photograph from above, cool fluorescent light on unfinished pine packing crates: each drawn outline becomes the upper rim of an open crate, placed inside the previous crate and smaller than it, all mouths facing upward. Straw, cloth, and tools lie only on the ledges between crates, while the deepest wooden mouth falls into shadow. No lids, markings, labels, or writing appear anywhere.

nesting.name: ice_fishing_holes
nesting.prompt_body: Aerial winter photograph of a frozen lake at blue hour: each drawn outline becomes the chipped edge of an ice hole cut through the surface, with a smaller dark opening visible farther down inside it, then another deeper opening below. Frost, slush, boot prints, and fishing gear remain on the shelves of ice between levels; the viewer's eye drops inward through the exposed water and never finds a covered end.

nesting.name: cut_cabbage
nesting.prompt_body: A macro studio photograph of a halved red cabbage on a slate board, lit with crisp side light: each drawn outline becomes a purple leaf edge encircling a smaller pale hollow farther inward, then another tighter leaf edge beyond. Moist veins and torn white ribs fill the spaces between levels, and the central part vanishes into a dark crevice, with no extra cuts or printed marks.

nesting.name: theater_arches
nesting.prompt_body: An oil painting in the style of a nineteenth century opera house backstage view, warm amber lamps and dusty velvet: each drawn outline becomes the painted edge of a proscenium arch, with another smaller arch visible through it, then another receding behind. Stage ropes, curtains, and wooden floorboards occupy the bands between openings; every arch remains uncovered, drawing the gaze deeper into the dim final stage.

nesting.name: cedar_bento
nesting.prompt_body: A Japanese woodblock print of stacked cedar lunch trays on a lacquer table, muted indigo, tan, and persimmon ink: each drawn outline becomes the raised lip of an uncovered tray, with a smaller empty tray set inside it, and another set deeper within. Rice grains, pickles, chopsticks, and folded cloth rest only between the lips, while the smallest tray is a dark interior with no lid or written decoration.

nesting.name: quarry_pits
nesting.prompt_body: A high altitude satellite view of an abandoned open quarry in ocher desert light: each drawn outline becomes the cut bench of a descending excavation, one ledge inside the last, shrinking toward a shadowed pit. Dirt roads, rusted machinery, puddles, and scrub occupy the terraces between benches, but no ramp climbs back outward; the composition leads step by step into the deepest exposed hollow.

nesting.name: lantern_tunnels
nesting.prompt_body: A long exposure night photograph inside a festival installation of square paper lantern frames, glowing crimson and gold: each drawn outline becomes one illuminated frame, and through its open center stands a smaller lit frame, then a farther one beyond. Visitors appear as faint blurs along the floor strips between frames, and the final small opening dissolves into darkness; there are no signs, arrows, or lettering.

symmetry.name: alpine_lake
symmetry.prompt_body: An aerial color photograph of a windless alpine lake at dawn: the central shoreline becomes the drawn middle stroke, the upper half of peaks, fir clusters, cabins, snow cracks and cloud wisps maps to the lower water image point by point. Every bend and small mark above the shore appears below in exact reverse order, with no boats, signs or writing.

symmetry.name: opera_stage
symmetry.prompt_body: A long exposure photograph inside a 1930s opera house, shot straight toward the stage: the central solo dancer becomes the drawn middle stroke, and the two drawn halves become rows of dancers, footlights, curtains and spotlight pools. Each pose, prop and lamp on the left returns on the right in backward order, matching height, spacing and angle, with an empty dark backdrop.

symmetry.name: market_still_life
symmetry.prompt_body: A Dutch golden age oil painting of a market table viewed square on: a tall brass candlestick at the center becomes the drawn middle stroke. The two drawn halves become pears, knives, folded cloth, grapes, clay cups and crumbs arranged left and right. Every object and tiny highlight on one side recurs across the candle in reverse order, without added items or written marks.

symmetry.name: desert_caravan
symmetry.prompt_body: A sepia panoramic photograph of a desert caravan crossing flat salt ground at noon: one standing guide and camel at center become the drawn middle stroke. The two drawn halves become camel silhouettes, footprints, water skins, shadows and low dunes. Each bend of a dune and each animal pose on one side is repeated on the other in backward order, sharply aligned.

symmetry.name: canal_fields
symmetry.prompt_body: A satellite view of irrigated farmland in late summer: the straight central canal becomes the drawn middle stroke, while the two drawn halves become crop plots, dirt roads, ponds, hay bales and tree rows. Every corner, culvert, field color and clump of trees west of the canal appears east of it in reverse order, with no map marks or labels.

symmetry.name: koi_pond_print
symmetry.prompt_body: A Japanese woodblock print of a quiet koi pond seen from above: one vertical reed stalk at center becomes the drawn middle stroke. The two drawn halves become koi, lily pads, fallen petals, ripples and stones. Each fish curve, leaf tear and petal cluster on the left is placed on the right in backward order, using indigo water, vermilion fish and pale cream paper.

symmetry.name: coral_tidepool
symmetry.prompt_body: A macro underwater photograph of a shallow tidepool in clear turquoise light: a straight blade of seagrass at center becomes the drawn middle stroke. The two drawn halves become coral branches, tiny fish, shells, bubbles and sand ridges. Every fork, shell chip and fish position on one side appears across the grass in backward order, held still by glassy water.

symmetry.name: hotel_staircase
symmetry.prompt_body: A crisp Art Deco architectural photograph of a grand double staircase in a marble hotel lobby, seen straight from the entrance: the vertical central carpet is the hinge, the left drawn half becomes one banister, landing edge, lamp row, and potted palms; the right drawn half repeats those same items in reverse order at equal distances, every kink and endpoint paired across the carpet. Warm amber lights, green marble, no people.

recursion.name: leaf_veins_macro
recursion.prompt_body: Shoot a macro photograph of a single translucent amber leaf on a light table: the thick midrib follows the trunk, and every drawn fork becomes a side vein splitting into smaller veinlets. Each child vein is thinner than its parent, following the drawn angle and length, ending in tiny pale tips. Exclude cross veins, holes, dew, insects, and any extra marks.

recursion.name: candle_wax_oil
recursion.prompt_body: Paint a classical oil still life of ivory candle wax running down a dark bronze holder: the main wax stream occupies the trunk, and every drawn fork becomes a split into two thinner rivulets. Each smaller rivulet follows the exact drawn direction, tapering until it ends as a bead of wax. Use warm lamplight, deep shadows, and no additional drips.

recursion.name: snow_paths_woodblock
recursion.prompt_body: Make a Japanese woodblock print of a snowy hillside at blue dusk: one dark trodden path rises from the lower edge where the trunk is, and every drawn fork becomes a fork in the footpath. The paths become narrower and lighter with each split, ending as tiny footprints at the tips. Preserve the unequal spacing and angles, with untouched snow elsewhere.

recursion.name: seaweed_ink
recursion.prompt_body: Create a spare sumi-e ink drawing of black seaweed on cream paper: the thick lower stalk stands where the trunk is, and every drawn fork becomes a split into slimmer seaweed fronds. Each frond tapers through the same drawn sequence until the smallest brush tips stop. Let ink density fade outward, but add no stray fronds, bubbles, stones, or calligraphy.

recursion.name: fiber_optic_long_exposure
recursion.prompt_body: Stage a long-exposure studio photograph of glowing fiber-optic cables on matte black cloth: the bright main cable follows the trunk, and every drawn fork becomes a Y-shaped connector sending light into thinner cables. Each cable dims and narrows as it proceeds to the next split, ending in tiny colored points. Keep all other cables hidden and avoid any extra crossings.

recursion.name: gold_thread_embroidery
recursion.prompt_body: Create a Victorian embroidery panel on deep green velvet: a thick raised gold cord follows the trunk, and every drawn fork becomes a sewn split into two finer gold threads. Each thread keeps the drawn bend, length, and uneven fork angle, then tapers to a small knot at the tip. Use subtle red silk shading, with no extra stitches outside the traced form.

recursion.name: red_coral_macro
recursion.prompt_body: Paint a luminous underwater macro photograph of red coral on dark teal water: one thick coral stalk rises where the trunk is, every fork in the guide becomes a fork in the coral, and each outgoing piece continues as a slimmer coral limb. The same two-way division repeats through larger limbs, smaller twigs, and finally tiny rounded polyps at the tips, with no extra offshoots, bubbles, fish, or text.

cycle.name: atoll_lagoon
cycle.prompt_body: A high-altitude satellite view of coral islets: every arc of the reference becomes a chain of separate sandy motu enclosing one turquoise lagoon; each pointed mark becomes a shallow channel notch aimed toward the next islet, all at the same distance from the calm middle water. The final channel opens back to the first beach with matching width, color, and scale, with no roads, signs, letters, or boats.

cycle.name: oak_year
cycle.prompt_body: A large-format photographic montage of the same oak in one meadow: every equal segment of the reference becomes one same-sized image placed about an empty sky-blue middle, early blossoms leading to dense green leaves, then orange foliage, then bare snowy branches, with windblown leaves showing the travel direction. The snowy image touches an early-blossom image identical in camera height and scale, no captions or borders with words.

cycle.name: mountain_water
cycle.prompt_body: A traditional black-ink landscape on rice paper: each curved part of the reference becomes one water event arranged about a blank misty center, sea vapor rising to clouds, clouds raining on mountains, rain entering brooks, brooks joining a river, the river reaching the sea. Each pointed mark becomes a brushstroke of flowing water aimed to the next event; the sea at the end matches the first sea wash exactly.

cycle.name: pollen_bees
cycle.prompt_body: A macro garden photograph with shallow focus: every bend of the reference becomes a trail of golden pollen grains between six different blossoms set about a soft dark middle; each pointed mark becomes a hovering bee angled toward the next flower. The last bee approaches the first blossom at the same height and size as the opening bee, with equal blossoms, natural dew, no tags, no printed marks.

cycle.name: candle_courtyard
cycle.prompt_body: A long-exposure night photograph in a stone courtyard: every segment of the reference becomes a person holding a plain wax candle, passing flame to the next person along a closed round path about the unlit fountain. Each pointed mark becomes a warm light streak from one wick to the next. The final streak lights the first candle from the same side and distance, all figures equally sized, no banners or writing.

cycle.name: tea_rain
cycle.prompt_body: An Edo-period woodblock print in indigo, moss green, and muted red: each section of the reference becomes one tea-making scene around a pale empty pond, rain feeding tea shrubs, hands picking leaves, steam softening leaves, rolled leaves drying, hot water brewing tea, steam rising to rainclouds. Each pointed mark becomes a drifting ribbon of vapor or leaf motion aimed onward; the last cloud matches the first raincloud in scale.

cycle.name: clay_workshop
cycle.prompt_body: Place four or more equal pottery-workshop stations in a clear one-way chain around an open floor, with no center table, wheel, kiln, or person dominating the scene. Start at a wet clay bowl, then move through throwing, glazing, firing, and shard grinding, using visible motion cues from one station to the next. The final station must return to the same wet clay bowl, unchanged in size, color, and viewpoint, so the path visibly comes back to its start.

cycle.name: crop_fields
cycle.prompt_body: A crisp aerial photograph of farm plots around a small round pond: each segment of the reference becomes one equal wedge of land, stubble, grazing sheep, dark plowed soil, new shoots, ripe grain, and cut stubble again. Each pointed mark becomes tractor tracks curving toward the next field. The last harvested wedge touches the first stubble wedge with identical tone and scale, no road signs, map marks, or numbers.

alternation.name: harbor_buoys
alternation.prompt_body: Along one taut floating rope in a calm harbor, place at least 8 round buoys evenly spaced from left to right, and make them alternate by color without exception: orange, white, orange, white, orange, white, orange, white. There must be only these two colors on the rope, no two neighboring buoys may match, no extra buoys may appear nearby, and the line should read clearly across the water in a natural seaside scene.

alternation.name: orchard_crates
alternation.prompt_body: A warm documentary photograph inside an old apple storehouse: each drawn node is a wooden fruit crate placed on the dusty floor, and each drawn link is a narrow plank touching the next crate. The crates switch without exception between two contents, bright red apples then pale green pears then red apples again, following the reference positions exactly, with bare floor around them and no signage.

alternation.name: reef_coral_markers
alternation.prompt_body: On a single gently curving trail in wet sand, place 10 small stones in one exact chain: lavender sponge-covered stone, bare cream limestone, lavender, cream, lavender, cream, lavender, cream, lavender, cream. Every stone must alternate one by one with no exception, so no two neighboring stones ever match and the last stone must be the opposite of the one before it. Keep the stones evenly spaced, same size, and make the beach otherwise calm and natural.

alternation.name: courtly_chess_pawns
alternation.prompt_body: A quiet oil painting in a Renaissance study, seen from above a walnut table: each drawn node becomes a carved chess pawn standing at the marked place, and each drawn link is a thin golden cord laid between neighboring pawns. The pawns are only ivory then ebony then ivory again, in strict turn from one end to the other, with no other chessmen present and no writing on the table.

alternation.name: tea_cups_woodblock
alternation.prompt_body: A Japanese woodblock print of a tea room shelf in muted indigo, tan, and cinnabar: every drawn node is a small teacup on the shelf, while each drawn link is the shelf edge segment connecting one cup to the next. The cups switch perfectly between blue glaze and unglazed brown clay, blue then brown then blue, with identical spacing from the reference and no extra cups elsewhere.

alternation.name: night_market_awning
alternation.prompt_body: Show a covered market walkway with at least 8 evenly spaced awning panels in a single row. The panels must follow one strict pattern with no exceptions: amber, blue, amber, blue, amber, blue, amber, blue, and so on, with no two adjacent panels ever matching and no third color anywhere. Keep the scene natural and photographic, with wet pavement reflections, hanging hardware between panels, and no signs, labels, or extra objects that could interrupt the sequence.

alternation.name: macaron_counter
alternation.prompt_body: On a glass pastry counter, place exactly 8 macarons in one straight line, evenly spaced from left to right. Their colors must switch with every single macaron: green, pink, green, pink, green, pink, green, pink. No two neighbors may share a color, and every second macaron must match the one two places away. Keep the scene realistic, with only the pastries, counter reflections, and soft shop lighting.

alternation.name: mountain_stepping_stones
alternation.prompt_body: A quiet Edo-period woodblock print of a narrow mountain stream crossed by flat stepping stones: every drawn node becomes one stone, ordered from foreground to misty distance, taking strict turns as dark wet basalt then pale dry granite, then dark basalt again. Each drawn segment is the visible strip of water between adjacent stones. The turn is unbroken across the whole crossing, with reeds and banks kept away from the stone centers, no writing or seals.

spiral.name: succulent_leaf_macro
spiral.prompt_body: A crisp macro photograph of a blue-green succulent seen from directly above: the row of leaf tips follows exactly the reference curve, the inner tip a tiny spear and each outward tip broader. Every drawn bend becomes a fleshy leaf edge, and each time the tips return to the same compass direction they sit a fixed ratio farther from the center, never matching an earlier scale.

spiral.name: vineyard_road
spiral.prompt_body: An autumn aerial photograph of a hillside vineyard: a pale service road follows exactly the reference curve through red and gold rows, starting at a small hut and widening outward across the slope. Every drawn segment becomes the road centerline between vines, and each time the road faces the same compass direction it lies a fixed ratio farther from the hut than the previous pass.

spiral.name: cinnamon_bun
spiral.prompt_body: A warm macro food photograph of a cinnamon bun on parchment: the dark cinnamon seam follows exactly the reference curve from the tight inner tuck to the broad outer crust. Every drawn bend becomes a glossy seam in the dough, and each time the seam points in the same compass direction it is a fixed ratio farther from the middle than before.

spiral.name: violin_pegbox
spiral.prompt_body: An old-master oil painting of a baroque violin pegbox on a velvet table: the raised maple ridge follows exactly the reference curve, beginning as a tight inner hook and growing into the outer cheek. Every drawn segment becomes a carved ridge with amber varnish, and each time it points the same compass direction it is a fixed ratio larger, never returning to an old size.

spiral.name: sea_eddy
spiral.prompt_body: A nineteenth-century Japanese woodblock print of a sea eddy beside black rocks: the white foam crest follows exactly the reference curve, starting at a dark calm eye and sweeping outward through indigo water. Every drawn bend becomes a jagged foam edge, and each time the crest reaches the same compass direction its distance from the eye has grown by the same ratio.

spiral.name: ram_horn
spiral.prompt_body: A sparse ink drawing of an old ram skull on handmade paper: the outer edge of one horn follows exactly the reference curve, from the small blunt core to the heavy weathered tip. Every drawn bend becomes a dark brush contour on horn keratin, and each time the contour returns to the same compass direction it is enlarged by one constant ratio.

spiral.name: ember_dancer
spiral.prompt_body: A night long-exposure photograph of a dancer on wet pavement: one ember trail follows exactly the reference curve, beginning near the dancer's hand and arcing outward in warm orange light. Every drawn segment becomes a continuous streak of fire, and each time the streak reaches the same compass direction it is a fixed ratio farther from the hand than on the prior pass.

spiral.name: carpet_vine
spiral.prompt_body: A studio close-up of an antique Persian carpet corner, where a single saffron vine winds outward from a tiny bud and completes at least three full turns. Each time the stem comes back to the same facing direction, it must be clearly larger by the same fixed ratio, so the third turn is unmistakably bigger than the second and the second bigger than the first. Keep the growth obvious, not a same-width coil.

bottleneck.name: mangrove_culvert
bottleneck.prompt_body: A high satellite view of two mangrove lagoons divided by a raised sand road: every drawn line inside the left cluster becomes a winding tidal creek among dark green roots, and every drawn line inside the right cluster becomes its own creek system. All water routes from one lagoon to the other squeeze through the same small culvert under the road, then spread outward again into separate channels. No boats, signs, labels, or markings.

bottleneck.name: courtyard_moon_gate
bottleneck.prompt_body: A late Qing courtyard painting in mineral greens and warm stone: each drawn branch on the left becomes a paved garden walk linking pavilions, wells, and bamboo beds; each drawn branch on the right becomes another set of walks among plum trees and benches. The two courtyards touch at one single round-topped doorway in the dividing wall, and every walk between sides passes through that doorway before splitting again. No calligraphy or seals.

bottleneck.name: ant_farm_throat
bottleneck.prompt_body: A macro photograph through glass of a vertical ant farm, amber sand against a dark studio background: every drawn segment in the upper colony becomes a clean tunnel joining several busy chambers, and every drawn segment in the lower colony becomes another connected set of tunnels. Between them is one narrow throat packed with ants; all travel from upper to lower chambers passes through that same throat, then fans into the lower tunnels. No labels or measuring marks.

bottleneck.name: rail_yard_switch
bottleneck.prompt_body: A 1930s industrial freight scene with two busy rail yards on opposite sides of a long warehouse wall. Each yard is densely interconnected with tracks, switches, sidings, sheds, and parked wagons. The only way from one yard to the other is a single narrow service opening in one central warehouse doorway; every crossing route must pass through that same opening, and there is no other bridge, gap, corridor, or passage anywhere else.

bottleneck.name: reef_cut
bottleneck.prompt_body: Every route from the left coral garden to the right coral garden must pass through one tiny notch in the pale sand ridge, and there is no other gap, tunnel, or shortcut anywhere. Inside each garden, many branching coral lanes and rock passages interconnect densely. The scene is a vivid underwater photograph: two rich reef clusters on either side of the ridge, with the single notch as the only place where fish can move from one side to the other.

bottleneck.name: market_arcade
bottleneck.prompt_body: Build the scene as two crowded market halls packed with many cross-aisles and side paths inside each hall, so shoppers can move around freely within the left half and within the right half. Between the two halls, include exactly one narrow stone archway and no other opening, gap, bridge, or side route. Every trip from one hall to the other must pass through that single archway, and if it were blocked, the two halls would remain separate but still fully walkable inside.

bottleneck.name: snowshoe_pass
bottleneck.prompt_body: A blue-hour aerial photograph of fresh snow over two forest clearings separated by a rocky ridge: each drawn line on the left becomes a packed snowshoe trail connecting cabins, woodpiles, and pines; each drawn line on the right becomes a separate web of trails around tents and sleds. All tracks between clearings merge at one low notch in the ridge, cross that notch, then split apart again. No signposts, words, or painted markers.

bottleneck.name: cave_lanterns
bottleneck.prompt_body: A chiaroscuro ink drawing of two limestone cave halls lit by hand lanterns: each drawn line in the upper hall becomes a dry walkway between stalagmites and pools, and each drawn line in the lower hall becomes its own connected set of walkways. The sole way from one hall to the other is a waist-high squeeze in the central rock wall; every walkway route passes through that squeeze before branching onward. No inscriptions or arrows.

convergence.name: rail_terminal
convergence.prompt_body: A crisp aerial photograph of a desert rail yard at sunrise: every drawn line is a steel track starting alone among scrub, each drawn fork is a switch where two tracks become one, and the united track ends at one roofed terminal shed with bumper posts. No rails continue beyond the shed, and there are no signs, letters, or labels.

convergence.name: pilgrim_temple
convergence.prompt_body: A misty mountain footpath scene with at least seven separate narrow trails starting far apart from different hamlets and terraces. Show each trail traveling independently, then joining only two at a time at clear stone crossings, so the merges are easy to count. Keep combining those shared paths until exactly one temple gate on the summit receives all of them. The gate is the final stop: sheer cliff, cloud, and empty sky lie beyond it, with no path continuing past.

convergence.name: ant_nest
convergence.prompt_body: A sharp macro nature photograph of pale sand: each drawn line is a dark trail of ants moving from its own crumb or seed, each drawn fork is where two ant columns meet and continue as one thicker column, and every column disappears into the same round nest entrance at the lower edge. No ants emerge past that hole, and the sand has no marks or lettering.

convergence.name: lightning_rod
convergence.prompt_body: A dramatic long-exposure night photograph over a lonely barn: the drawn upper tips are separate cloud patches, each drawn line is a bright lightning channel, each drawn fork is where two channels meet and continue as one, and the last channel ends on a single metal rod atop the roof. The strike stops there, with black fields beyond and no signs or words.

convergence.name: paint_cup
convergence.prompt_body: A studio macro photograph of a tilted white enamel tray: each drawn line is a ribbon of colored paint sliding from its own drip at the rim, each drawn fork is the wet place where ribbons mix and become a wider stream, and all paint pours into one small cup at the lower edge and stops there. The tabletop beyond is clean, with no writing.

convergence.name: ski_lodge
convergence.prompt_body: Show a snowy mountain slope with at least six separate ski tracks beginning far apart on different ridges. The tracks descend independently, then meet in visible pairings and combine into fewer tracks until every line ends at one single lodge doorway at the bottom. The doorway is the only endpoint: all tracks stop there and nothing continues past it. Use a Japanese woodblock look with cobalt shadows and vermilion accents, but no signs, captions, or people.

convergence.name: mill_belts
convergence.prompt_body: A documentary photograph inside an old textile mill: each drawn line is a narrow cloth conveyor coming from a separate loom, each drawn fork is a transfer table where two belts feed one belt, and the last belt drops all fabric into one open packing crate at the back wall. No belt exits the crate, and the walls and machines carry no visible lettering.

convergence.name: candle_wax
convergence.prompt_body: Show six or more separate wax drips starting far apart on a long candlelit table, each drip beginning at its own candle and traveling on its own narrow metal channel. Let the channels join only two at a time, then join again, until every stream ends in one small stone cup at the center. The cup is the final stop: wax collects there and nothing continues past it. Keep it like a real still life, with no labels or diagram style.

symmetry_breaking.name: broken_solar_panel
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A crisp modern satellite image of a desert solar farm: every drawn square becomes one identical blue-black panel, set at the same tilt and distance across the whole view, except at the drawn black circle, where exactly one panel is pale and shattered. All other panels stay intact, equal in size, and evenly placed, with bare sand between them.

symmetry_breaking.name: red_beach_umbrella
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A bright midday aerial photograph of a crowded beach seen straight down: every drawn square becomes one closed yellow umbrella with the same shadow and spacing on clean sand, except at the drawn black circle, where exactly one umbrella is open and crimson. Towels, footprints, and waves stay outside the repeated area, leaving all other umbrellas identical.

symmetry_breaking.name: burnt_bun
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A warm macro photograph of a bakery cooling rack: every drawn square becomes one glossy sesame bun, same size, same golden crust, placed in orderly rows, except at the drawn black circle, where exactly one bun is charred black. The metal rack is plain and clean, and no other bun is split, tilted, darker, or missing.

symmetry_breaking.name: blue_roof_tile
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A flat-color Japanese woodblock print of a broad temple roof: every drawn square becomes one terracotta roof tile, all facing the same way and cut to the same size, except at the drawn black circle, where exactly one tile is glazed cobalt blue. The sky is empty, the roof edge is straight, and every other tile remains red clay.

symmetry_breaking.name: dark_lit_window
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A long-exposure night photograph of a glass apartment facade: every drawn square becomes one warm lit window, all equal in shape and brightness, stacked across the wall, except at the drawn black circle, where exactly one window is dark with a single red curtain visible. Reflections are faint and uniform, and every other window glows the same amber.

symmetry_breaking.name: empty_seed_cell
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A soft natural-light photograph of a greenhouse seed tray from above: every drawn square becomes one dark soil cell holding the same tiny pair of green leaves, except at the drawn black circle, where exactly one cell is bare dry soil. The tray walls are clean, the leaves match in height, and no second cell is empty or wilted.

symmetry_breaking.name: black_teacup
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A contemporary overhead studio photograph of porcelain teacups on a white table: every drawn square becomes one cup filled with clear pale tea, identical handle direction and spacing, except at the drawn black circle, where exactly one cup holds opaque black coffee. The saucers are all plain white, and every other cup remains unchanged.

symmetry_breaking.name: salt_pan_anomaly
symmetry_breaking.prompt_body: A photorealistic aerial photograph of a vast salt farm arranged in a strict array of shallow rectangular basins: every drawn square becomes one pale basin with thin silver water and white crusted edges, and every drawn line becomes a straight earthen dike between basins. At the drawn black circle, one basin is flooded with vivid rose brine and a single blue tarp, the only departure anywhere.

self_reference.name: camera_lcd
self_reference.prompt_body: A crisp late-1990s color photograph in a small apartment studio: the outermost rectangle is the printed photo edge, the next rectangle is the camera back, and the innermost rectangle is the glowing LCD. That LCD shows this exact photo’s event: the same hands holding the same camera at this instant, with the same LCD content reduced to a single bright patch, not readable as another scene, no lettering anywhere.

self_reference.name: tailor_sampler
self_reference.prompt_body: A framed embroidery hoop hanging above the antique tailor’s worktable must show a clear miniature view of this exact room: the same cream linen cloth, rust border, indigo panels, scissors, thimble, and spool in the same positions, so the picture reads as the whole scene seen again once. Keep it natural and realistic, with no text, labels, or diagram look, and no second copy inside the copy.

self_reference.name: greenhouse_pane
self_reference.prompt_body: A rainy Edwardian greenhouse scene painted in soft oil colors: the outer rectangle is the glass wall seen head-on, the next rectangle is a fogged pane cleaned by a gardener’s sleeve, and the remaining rectangles are pane edges within that clear area. The cleared pane contains a painted view of this exact greenhouse wall, gardener, plants, and wiped pane, matching every object placement, with its carried view stopping as wet glass shimmer.

self_reference.name: market_awning
self_reference.prompt_body: A sunlit aerial photograph of a seaside produce market, teal shadows and orange crates: the outermost rectangle is the whole plaza boundary, the next rectangle is a striped vendor awning, and the inner rectangle is a printed cloth laid on that stall. The cloth image is the same plaza seen from above, including that stall, awning, crates, and cloth, agreeing item for item; the cloth’s own center becomes plain woven color, no words.

self_reference.name: chocolate_plaque
self_reference.prompt_body: A framed picture in the scene must show the entire same kitchen-counter scene, not just the chocolate bar: the ivory-and-espresso counter, parchment, bitten chocolate bar with almond flecks, warm lighting, and the same frame and background objects all visible together in the picture. The picture should be clearly recognizable as a copy of this whole view, and nothing inside that picture should show the scene again. Keep it as a natural tabletop still life with no text, labels, or diagram-like styling.

self_reference.name: salt_barge
self_reference.prompt_body: A cozy sunlit living room in warm beige and teal. The key requirement is a framed picture on the wall that clearly shows this same living room from the same angle: the same sofa, floor lamp, window, rug, coffee table, and plant, all arranged exactly like the real scene so it reads as the whole image inside the frame. Inside that framed picture, there is no smaller copy and no extra frame, only the single plain room view. No text or labels.

self_reference.name: puppet_booth

That backdrop depicts this exact booth, the same red curtains, carved fox puppet, puppeteer's hands, candles, and backdrop; every remaining drawn rectangle is that depicted backdrop returning to the visible backdrop, not another tiny stage.

self_reference.name: sushi_tray
self_reference.prompt_body: A top-down Meiji-style sushi-tray scene in indigo, salmon, and rice-paper cream. The main tray, chopsticks, ginger pile, rice grains, and seaweed sheet all appear exactly once. On the tray, a small framed print shows the entire same scene again from the same angle: the same tray, same food, same composition, clearly recognizable as the whole image itself. That framed copy is only one level deep and contains no smaller copy inside it.

strange_loop.name: newsroom_desks
strange_loop.prompt_body: The main line of the scene must be one unbroken newsroom path: a ground-floor copy desk rises through stacked desk tiers and balcony-like platforms, then the highest tier turns into a narrow catwalk that visibly descends back and lands on that same copy desk where it began. The return connection must be clear and dominant. Photorealistic black-and-white 1940s newsroom, with filing cabinets, desk lamps, ashtrays, and paper stacks.

strange_loop.name: court_bench
strange_loop.prompt_body: Make the main composition a single visible ascent that returns to its start: in a courthouse interior, a clerk sits at the lowest bench, a bailiff stands one step above, a judge presides on a raised dais, and a lord watches from an upper gallery. One continuous wooden stair, railing, and balcony path must carry the eye all the way up, then through the top opening and back down to land beside the clerk’s bench where it began. Ukiyo-e woodblock print, indigo and vermilion, late Edo mood.

strange_loop.name: radio_booth
strange_loop.prompt_body: A midnight radio studio whose main composition is one continuous, traceable path: start at the floor host booth, climb through glass editing booths, then balconies, then a raised control screen, and at the very top the path must visibly come back down and land beside the same host booth where it began. The top screen should show the original floor room below, and a clear stair or catwalk must connect top to bottom in plain sight. No signage, no diagrams, just the studio space.

strange_loop.name: glasshouse_bench
strange_loop.prompt_body: A single traceable path must climb from the damp potting bench on the ground floor to an upper catwalk, then continue into a glazed screen that shows the same bench below, so the highest level visibly returns to the start. In a warm Victorian greenhouse, gardeners, the curator, and the patron occupy each step and platform, each speaking about the next person up, while iron uprights, hanging ferns, and benches guide the eye along the returning route.

strange_loop.name: apartment_walkways
strange_loop.prompt_body: Make the entire scene one continuous apartment-building climb that visibly returns to its starting point: an exterior stairway and balconies rise from the ground-floor courtyard to the top terrace, then the same stairway continues and descends back into that very courtyard, ending at the same entrance landing where it began. Keep this return path obvious, unbroken, and dominant in the composition. Show everyday residents, railings, windows, and warm evening light in a realistic hillside apartment block.

strange_loop.name: museum_carts
strange_loop.prompt_body: In a museum storage room, make one continuous stair-and-catwalk path the main shape of the scene: it begins at a rolling cart on the floor, climbs through three stacked storage levels, and the top landing must connect back to that same cart with a visible stair or ramp that lands where it started. The highest shelf, bridge, and lower cart should be one unbroken route. A registrar on the cart speaks about a restorer, the restorer about a curator, and the curator back about the registrar.

strange_loop.name: hotel_doors
strange_loop.prompt_body: A small apartment stairwell must show one continuous, traceable route that rises through stairs, landings, and balcony railings, and the highest landing must visibly return to the exact bottom foyer by the same path, like a stair that climbs up and then lands where it began. The viewer should be able to follow the route without interruption from the entrance to the top and back to the starting tile. Everyday interior, warm morning light, no text or signs.

strange_loop.name: theater_catwalk
strange_loop.prompt_body: Make the scene’s main structure a single visible stairway path that climbs from a dressing-room floor to an upper catwalk, then turns and comes back down to the exact same doorway where it started, so the top level clearly returns to the bottom in one traceable path. Keep it as a backstage theater with dusty rose walls, black ropes, work lights, and wooden railings. On the lower landing, an actor speaks about the director, the director about the playwright, and the playwright about the actor.

isomorphism.name: harbor_tram_depot

On the left, a fishing harbor: one quay leads to four piers, with the same two side slips and the same two final berths in the same order. isomorphism.name: rice_suburb

isomorphism.name: seaweed_silk_shop

isomorphism.name: cave_rail_yard

Each split on one side must line up with the matching split on the other, in the same layout, only the material changes from rock to steel and gravel. No labels or signs.

isomorphism.name: salt_parking_lot

The left basins are cut by thin raised ridges into smaller basins, while the right asphalt is cut by painted islands into smaller bays; every fork in a channel becomes a fork in a lane, and every corner of a basin becomes a corner of a parking island.

isomorphism.name: vineyard_village

isomorphism.name: filtration_corridor

The linework keeps every turn and split in step.

isomorphism.name: promenade_assembly_aisle
isomorphism.prompt_body: A chromogenic photograph of a coastal promenade on the left and a factory assembly aisle on the right, shot in bright overcast light. The promenade's railings split around each lookout recess exactly where the assembly aisle splits around each workbench island; every bench alcove matches one overlook, and every short spur from the path matches one short spur from the aisle. Nothing is added, removed, or shifted.

figure_ground.name: rice_paddies
figure_ground.prompt_body: Build the rice terraces so each dark flooded plot and each pale mist-filled gap share one exact contour and both read as real paddy shapes, not background: the empty channels must be as clearly shaped as the muddy fields. Dawn aerial view, muddy earth, silver haze, soft green fields.

figure_ground.name: salt_basins

The dark and light shapes should both read as real connected forms, like interlocking birds and fish, not mere cracks. Chalk white, turquoise, dusty rose, crisp noon light, no extra land.

figure_ground.name: vineyard_hills

Late-1970s color film, rust, gold, plum, deep green.

figure_ground.name: shipyard_night
figure_ground.prompt_body: Make the night shipping yard do the job: the dark container stacks, crane booms, and aisle turns must be readable as one set of solid shapes, and the light gaps between them must read as the same stacks, booms, and turns using the exact same outlines. Pack the frame edge to edge so the upper half’s black forms return in the lower half as bright empty bays, with the same scene order preserved, not reversed or repeated as texture.

figure_ground.name: fish_racks
figure_ground.prompt_body: Make the whole print a rack of drying fish where every dark fish shape is matched by a fish-shaped pale gap, and every gap reads as a second fish, so the page is filled edge to edge with interlocking fish silhouettes. In the upper half, dark fish hang in rows with pale fish-shaped openings between them; in the lower half, that exact head-to-tail arrangement returns as pale fish with dark fish-shaped openings, not just a color swap. 1930s Japanese woodblock, indigo, bone, vermilion, crisp carved edges.

figure_ground.name: laundry_courtyard
figure_ground.prompt_body: Fill the whole frame with one laundry courtyard that reads in both directions at once: the dark shirts, sheets, and towels hanging across the upper half must have bright counterparts below with the exact same outlines, as if the lower half were cut from soot-dark walls and the gaps were also shirts and sheets. Keep the poles, cloth folds, and spacing in the same order throughout, so no part feels like empty background.

figure_ground.name: mushroom_trays
figure_ground.prompt_body: Make the entire cellar read as interlocking mushroom caps and mushroom-shaped gaps, so the dark spaces are not background but clear cap forms with the same outline as the pale caps. Every tray gap should also look like a mushroom, and every mushroom shape should have a matching dark counterpart, filling the full frame. In the upper half, pale caps sit against dark compost; in the lower half, the same scene continues with those exact shapes taking the opposite tones in the same order. Cold blue, cream, earthy brown, damp and intimate.

figure_ground.name: canal_roofs
figure_ground.prompt_body: In a canal-side street, the upper half must turn into the lower half’s pale cottage shapes, and the upper half’s gaps must become the lower half’s dark cottages, keeping the same left-to-right order. Every roofline, wall, and chimney outline should be readable as a house in both colors, so the light spaces are not background but houses too. Make the dark and light cottages lock together across the full frame in an Edo woodblock print palette of indigo, soot black, and bone white.

mobius.name: film_strip
mobius.prompt_body: The film strip must have one unmistakable half-twist: one visible section where the front surface turns over into the back surface, with the two sides clearly different in color and texture, and the strip crossing itself once before reaching the clamp again. After one full trip around the strip, the printed side should come back flipped left-to-right; only after a second trip should it match exactly. Close-up archival photo on a black table, no labels.

mobius.name: paper_streamer
mobius.prompt_body: Color woodblock print in an Edo-like style of a wide paper streamer pinned across a room as the drawn form: the long edges become the trimmed paper edges, and each crosspiece becomes a pasted fold mark. The streamer makes one half-turn at the upper bend, so the painted face and the plain backside exchange places while the ends are tied to a small nail.

mobius.name: conveyor_belt
mobius.prompt_body: An industrial conveyor belt in a packing plant must visibly make one clear half-twist: the band rises, twists once so the bright rubber face turns into a dark, textured backside, then continues around and meets itself with the faces swapped, so one full pass returns to the start with left and right exchanged, while two passes would restore the original side. Keep it a realistic photo with rollers, guards, and worn rubber texture.

mobius.name: packing_strap
mobius.prompt_body: Realist oil painting of a plastic packing strap draped over a warehouse pallet as the drawn form: the two long edges become the strap edges, and the crosspieces become tiny molded ridges. A single half-turn near the center sends the shiny face to the dull face, and the strap returns to the clip from the far side without breaking.

mobius.name: boardwalk
mobius.prompt_body: A marsh boardwalk made from one continuous wooden strip must have one unmistakable half-twist: at a single point, the sun-bleached top boards visibly roll over and become the darker underside, with the rail and plank edges swapping sides so both faces are seen in one view. The walkway should clearly reconnect as a twisted ring over the water, not a flat oval, so one trip around returns to the start with left and right reversed, while two trips restore the original orientation.

mobius.name: seat_belt
mobius.prompt_body: A parked-car interior photo of a seat belt hanging from the upper anchor to the buckle, but the strap must show one obvious half-twist: along one section the stitched tan front face turns over and becomes the darker, rough back face, with both faces clearly visible side by side and the twist visible edge-on. After that single flip, the strap continues back to the buckle so the belt is a twisted band, not a flat ring.

mobius.name: wool_scarf
mobius.prompt_body: Soft charcoal drawing in a 19th-century sketchbook style of a wool scarf draped over a chair as the drawn form: the two long edges become the knitted edges, and each crosspiece becomes a row of knit ribs. A single half-turn in the center sends the fuzzy outside to the inside and back again as the ends are pinned together with a clasp.

mobius.name: glass_hothouse_walkway
mobius.prompt_body: Inside a Victorian conservatory, the main raised garden walkway is one wide ribbon that visibly makes a single half-turn before joining itself: at one point the walking surface flips over so the pale flowered top becomes a dark stone underside, and the two faces have clearly different colors and textures. A gardener standing on that crossover appears upside down relative to the rest of the path. Walking it once returns you facing backward; two passes restore the original facing. Do not show a second level or ordinary oval ring.

braiding.name: silk_ribbons
braiding.prompt_body: A close macro photograph in late-afternoon light of three silk ribbons lying across a worn pine tabletop. The traced path from the left edge is followed exactly: the crimson ribbon goes over the ivory ribbon, then under the teal one; the ivory ribbon then crosses over the teal and later slips beneath the crimson at the next meeting. At the right edge, the three ends are in a different vertical order than at the start, matching the full chain of crossings.

braiding.name: vine_trellis
braiding.prompt_body: Three vine stems must be visible the whole time, and they must cross in a repeated over-under weave at several points, with each crossing clearly showing one stem on top and the other two underneath or swapping positions. Do not let it look like only two stems. Keep the stems separate enough that all three can be traced from left to right along the weathered garden fence, with small leaves attached, and end with a different left-to-right order than they began.

braiding.name: garden_hoses
braiding.prompt_body: A sunlit courtyard photograph of three rubber garden hoses draped across a stone trough. The hoses follow the supplied path line for line: one hose rides over the next at the first crossing, then disappears beneath it at the next, while the third trades places in the same stepwise manner. Metal nozzles mark the ends. The hose ends on the far side arrive in a new top-to-bottom order, produced only by the crossings.

braiding.name: seaweed_fronds
braiding.prompt_body: A Japanese woodblock print in muted green and indigo of three long seaweed fronds laid on black wet rocks at low tide. Each frond follows the marked sweep across the stone, with one frond passing over another at every contact and then under it at the next contact. Tiny foam patches sit beside the crossings. At the right-hand edge, the fronds emerge in a changed left-to-right order compared with the left.

braiding.name: fishing_lines
braiding.prompt_body: A long-exposure night photograph on a harbor pier: three taut fishing lines, lit by small lanterns, arc exactly along the reference path above the dark water. At each crossing, the nearest line passes over the other, then drops beneath at the next. Floats and hooks are placed only at the ends. The lines leave the frame in a different vertical order than they entered, so the eye can read the whole exchange from left to right.

braiding.name: prayer_banners
braiding.prompt_body: A temple-courtyard fresco in faded mineral colors of three narrow prayer banners stretched between poles. The cloth strips follow the prescribed route with no deviation: the saffron strip crosses over the blue, then under the white; the blue then takes its turn over and under in the next contact. Wind flutter is slight, not enough to alter the path. The far ends show a new order from the near ends.

braiding.name: workshop_cables
braiding.prompt_body: A gritty workshop photograph of three insulated electrical cables draped across a pegboard and over two hooks. The right-side cable ends are not in the same stack order as the left-side ends, because the crossing sequence has been carried out in full.

braiding.name: river_reeds
braiding.prompt_body: Three or more long reed stalks must be the main focus, and they must visibly cross each other several times in a clear over-under order, with each crossing easy to read from the scene. Show the stalks laid across a muddy riverbank with water, pebbles, and fallen seeds nearby. Keep every stalk separate at both ends, and make the end arrangement different from the starting order because of the repeated crossings. Do not let it look like just two strands twisting together.

interference.name: rice_paddy
interference.prompt_body: Aerial photograph of a flooded rice paddy at dawn, seen straight down: the two drawn centers become two sprinkler heads sending tiny waves across the water between young shoots. Each drawn circle becomes a pale line on the surface, and where the two sets cross, brighter and dimmer bands appear with a wider spacing than either source alone. Keep the two origins slightly offset exactly as shown.

interference.name: soup_bowl
interference.prompt_body: Macro photograph of a ceramic soup bowl on a wooden table after two spoon tips touch the broth at the two drawn points: each drawn circle becomes a faint wave on the glossy surface. Two sets spread outward and cross, making pale and dark bands that settle into a slower spacing than either spoon made alone. Use cool green glaze, 1980s kitchen lighting, and a quiet tabletop setting.

interference.name: courtyard_cistern
interference.prompt_body: Woodblock print of a courtyard cistern at dusk, with dark eaves above and still water below: the two drawn centers are two roof drips falling into the cistern, and each drawn circle becomes a sharp white arc in the water. The two sets spread, meet, and leave broad light and dark bands that sit farther apart than either drip spacing. Use indigo, bone, and rust with a Meiji-era feel.

interference.name: fountain_basin
interference.prompt_body: 19th-century oil painting of a public fountain basin in a stone courtyard: the two drawn centers are two fingertip touches on the water, and each drawn circle becomes a soft marble-colored wave. The two sets cross and leave alternating bright and shadowed bands that open wider than either touch alone. Warm ochres, wet slate, and late-afternoon sun give the scene a quiet, formal mood.

interference.name: station_puddle
interference.prompt_body: Long-exposure color photograph of a station puddle under a neon awning after the first rain: the two drawn centers are two drops from a leaking gutter, and each drawn circle becomes a pale smear on the black water. The two sets cross into broad luminous and dark bands with a spacing larger than either drip could make alone. Use magenta, cyan, and tar-black for a late-night city feel.

interference.name: salt_pan
interference.prompt_body: Monochrome ink drawing of a salt pan seen from above: the two drawn centers are two brine drips from a cracked pipe, and each drawn circle becomes a thin wash line on the flat water skin. As the two sets spread and meet, they leave wider pale and dark bands than either drip spacing. Keep the strokes spare, with dry paper texture and hard midday shadows.

interference.name: reservoir_inlet
interference.prompt_body: Satellite-style aerial photograph of a reservoir inlet at midday: the two drawn centers are two maintenance boats leaving small wakes from different points, and each drawn circle becomes a pale curve on the green water. The two wake sets cross and produce broader bright and dim bands that return more slowly than either boat wake alone. Cool teal, algae green, and sun-faded concrete anchor the view.

interference.name: bakery_glaze
interference.prompt_body: Macro photograph of a shallow pastry glaze tray in a bakery: the two drawn centers are two spoonfuls of water dropped onto the shiny icing, and each drawn circle becomes a faint clear line in the amber surface. The two sets cross, making wide pale and shadowed bands that spread farther apart than either drop alone. Soft tungsten light, honey, cream, and copper finish the scene.

tiling.name: greenhouse_plots
tiling.prompt_body: A contemporary aerial photograph of a glass greenhouse farm at dawn: each drawn six-sided cell becomes one raised planting bed filled with lettuce, herbs, and dark soil, the narrow seams between beds become thin wet walkways, and the clipped beds at the frame edges match the reference exactly. Cool mist, pale green leaves, and steel frames keep the view practical and real.

tiling.name: terracotta_roof

tiling.name: archive_boxes

tiling.name: courtyard_pavers
tiling.prompt_body: A tea house courtyard after rain fills the entire frame with identical wet stone pavers in a repeating grid; every paver has the same shape, size, tone, and sheen, and every seam is a thin line of moss or pooled water. tiling.name: fruit_crates
tiling.prompt_body: A 1950s color lithograph of a produce warehouse: every drawn cell becomes one wooden apple crate filled with green fruit, the gaps between crates become the slits of the pallets beneath, and the crates at the margins are clipped exactly like the reference. tiling.name: lantern_ceiling

tiling.name: laundry_baskets

tiling.name: reading_cubbies
tiling.prompt_body: A Victorian etching of a reading room wall of cubby shelves: every drawn cell becomes one open cubby holding a single worn book or folded scarf, each seam becomes the thin wood divider, and the cubbies at the frame edges are clipped exactly as shown. hub.name: traffic_roundabout

hub.name: desert_well

hub.name: brass_chandelier

hub.name: garden_parasol

hub.name: mooring_bollard

hub.name: laundry_pole

hub.name: ceiling_fan

hub.name: coat_stand

infinite_descent.name: desert_water_jars
infinite_descent.prompt_body: A sun-bleached documentary photograph in a dry courtyard. Every drawn horizontal stair tread becomes a sandstone step holding one clay water jar, each jar strictly smaller than the jar on the step above; every drawn vertical fall is the sharp stair face between them. infinite_descent.name: rice_paddy_pools
infinite_descent.prompt_body: A high aerial photograph of misty mountain rice terraces after rain. infinite_descent.name: dew_on_leaves

infinite_descent.name: altar_candles

The largest version must be hidden above the top frame, and the smallest visible one must still continue downward out of the bottom edge. The viewer should never see a first candle or a complete starting scene, only a chain of smaller and smaller copies disappearing beyond the frame.

infinite_descent.name: harbor_boats
infinite_descent.prompt_body: Show a row of the same kind of fishing boat stepping downward along a steep harbor slipway, each boat clearly smaller than the one above it.
