Keep the boats aligned in one continuous descent through wet planks, indigo water, rusted wood, and foam white.

infinite_descent.name: porcelain_teacups
infinite_descent.prompt_body: A fine ink-and-wash still life on cream paper. Every drawn horizontal stair tread becomes a lacquered shelf supporting one plain porcelain teacup, each cup strictly smaller than the cup above; every drawn vertical fall becomes the dark shelf side. Each cup is tipped so its open side faces the next lower cup. The drawn hard floor is an empty tabletop under the smallest cup, which tips toward bare wood, with no decorative writing.

infinite_descent.name: cave_lanterns
infinite_descent.prompt_body: Hide the largest lantern completely above the ceiling beam so the visible row begins in the middle, with no first lantern shown. In a dim cave stairwell, place one glass lantern on each step, all the same shape and style, and make each lantern strictly smaller than the one above it. The row should keep descending past the bottom edge, with the last lantern partly clipped out of frame, and there must be no base, stopper, or end marker anywhere.

infinite_descent.name: market_baskets
infinite_descent.prompt_body: Show a row of woven produce baskets on an empty market stair, each basket forcing the next lower basket to be visibly smaller, with the larger basket opening toward it like it has to give way. The biggest basket must be cut off by the top edge or hidden behind a pillar, and the smaller baskets keep continuing out of the frame below, so no first basket is visible. The chain continues past both edges.

infinite_descent.name: glacier_ice_blocks
infinite_descent.prompt_body: Show a kitchen counter with a row of identical white mixing bowls that get strictly smaller one by one, but the largest bowl is not visible because it is cut off behind a cabinet edge or hidden by a hanging towel. The visible bowls begin in the middle of the size chain and continue out of the frame, so there is no first bowl anywhere in view. Make the size steps discrete and unmistakable: each bowl is a whole step smaller than the next.

coprime_orbit.name: woven_basket_lip
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A warm macro photograph of an unfinished willow basket mouth: the drawn outer points become ten pierced holes in the cane edge. One pale reed is woven as a single strand, always skipping two holes and entering the third, crossing the open mouth in straight taut runs. It touches every hole once before returning to the starting hole, with the empty interior left untouched.

coprime_orbit.name: plaza_lantern_pass
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A night long-exposure photograph in a stone plaza: the drawn outer points become eight dancers standing in a wide round formation, each holding still except for one amber lantern being passed. The light trail always flies past two dancers to the third, making one uninterrupted glowing path that reaches all eight hands before coming back to the first, with no person in the middle.

coprime_orbit.name: salt_pan_channels
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A crisp aerial view of coastal salt pans at noon: the drawn outer points become twelve pale round basins set around a flat white field. One turquoise sluice route is the only colored watercourse, always passing four dry basins and entering the fifth. Raised crossings keep overlapping stretches separate; the water reaches every basin once before returning to its first basin, and there is no central reservoir.

coprime_orbit.name: glass_jewel_window
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A backlit photograph of a handmade cathedral window without figures: the drawn outer points become eleven ruby glass beads set along the outer iron frame. A single continuous golden lead strip steps past three beads and joins the fourth each time, crossing the clear blue glass in long straight spans. Every bead is touched once before the strip returns to the first, leaving the middle pane clear.

coprime_orbit.name: maple_pond_cord
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A quiet ukiyo-e woodblock print of a temple pond in autumn: the drawn outer points become nine black bamboo stakes placed around the water. A single vermilion festival cord runs from stake to stake, always skipping one stake and tying onto the second. The cord forms one continuous journey over the pond, visiting all nine stakes before arriving back where it began; fallen maple leaves float below.

coprime_orbit.name: banquet_red_sash
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: Place 12 candles evenly around a round dinner table. One single gold ribbon must travel from candle to candle by a fixed jump of 5 seats each time, skipping the ones in between, so the chords crisscross into a sharp star shape and the ribbon reaches every candle exactly once before coming back to the start. Do not add any center post, extra strands, labels, or adjacent linking.

coprime_orbit.name: cliff_shrine_bridges
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A monochrome ink wash drawing of a high mountain basin: the drawn outer points become thirteen tiny cliff shrines spaced along the surrounding ledges. One black brush stroke of suspended footbridges always skips three shrines and reaches the fourth, crossing the misty void in straight spans. The route visits every shrine before returning to the first, with open white mist occupying the middle.

coprime_orbit.name: dew_grass_filament
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A close-up dawn scene of seven dew-bright grass seed heads arranged evenly around a perfect circle, like markers on a round wreath. One single spider silk makes the only path: it starts at one seed head, then always skips the next head and lands on the following one, repeating the same step all the way around. The strand crosses the open center, touches every bead exactly once, and returns to the start with no extra strands.

coprime_orbit.name: bath_floor_mosaic
coprime_orbit.prompt_body: A Byzantine-style mosaic floor seen from above in an old bathhouse: the drawn outer points become twelve turquoise scallop shells set into cream stone. One uninterrupted path of gold tesserae always skips four shells and meets the fifth, creating crisp straight bands across the floor. It reaches every shell once before returning to the first shell, and the central tiles remain plain ivory.

pigeonhole.name: mail_sort_wall
pigeonhole.prompt_body: A quiet photorealistic post office workroom at dawn with no writing anywhere: each drawn box is one open wooden mail slot in a sorting wall, and each drawn upper point is a plain cream envelope on the counter. Every drawn line becomes the slid paper trail and final placement of an envelope into its assigned slot. There are exactly nine envelopes and eight slots; one unmarked slot holds two envelopes, all others hold one.

pigeonhole.name: harbor_dinghy_slips
pigeonhole.prompt_body: Show seven small white dinghies moving toward six visible marina slips, with all six slips already occupied or clearly reserved by another boat so the shortage is obvious at a glance. The dinghies are still mid-approach, clustered close enough that at least one pair must end up sharing a slip, but do not reveal which pair; keep several boats equally near the same dock area, with no labels, arrows, or highlighted point.

pigeonhole.name: dumpling_sauce_bowls
pigeonhole.prompt_body: Overhead on a dark wooden table, show nine small porcelain bowls as the visible slots and ten steamed dumplings moving toward them at once. Every bowl already has one dumpling pressed against its rim or partly in it, so the tenth dumpling has to share a bowl with another; keep at least two dumplings equally close to the same bowl so no single pair is singled out. Make the 10-to-9 imbalance obvious at a glance. No empty bowl, no extra bowl, no neat two-row lineup.

pigeonhole.name: orchard_crate_harvest
pigeonhole.prompt_body: Warm rustic oil painting of an orchard floor after picking: each drawn box is a low wooden apple crate, each drawn upper point is a fallen red apple, and each drawn line becomes a curved roll mark in dusty soil ending at a crate. Paint exactly eight apples and seven crates. One plain crate contains two apples while the other crates contain one, with no worker pointing or sorting.

pigeonhole.name: theater_mask_pegs
pigeonhole.prompt_body: An old backstage cloak wall shows eleven theater masks in motion toward ten visible pegs, with every peg already occupied, so at least one arriving mask must end up sharing a peg. Make the imbalance obvious at a glance: more masks than pegs, all pegs claimed, several masks equally close to the same few pegs, but do not point to any single pair. Keep it as a lively woodblock print with curtains, ropes, and props in the background, not a labeled or diagram-like layout.

pigeonhole.name: apiary_landing_slots
pigeonhole.prompt_body: Show a calm beekeeper’s wall with exactly six clearly visible hive entrance slots in a row, and seven bees in the air moving toward them. All six slots should already look claimed, while the seventh bee has to crowd in with another bee at one of the same openings. Keep several bees equally close to the same few slots so the shared landing place is obvious by count, but do not point to any single pair. Ink-and-wash style, natural and quiet.

pigeonhole.name: tram_depot_bays
pigeonhole.prompt_body: Show a flat side-view of a small tram depot where the counting is obvious at a glance: four open service bays are already filled by four trams, and five more trams are arriving in the yard at the same time, so every bay is claimed and one incoming tram must end up sharing a bay nose-to-tail with another. Keep several arrivals equally close to the occupied bays; do not spotlight any single pair.

pigeonhole.name: pottery_kiln_cubbies
pigeonhole.prompt_body: In a soft natural-light ceramic studio photo, show 13 wet clay pots moving toward 12 visible kiln-shelf cubbies. Every cubby already has one pot, while the last pots are still in hands and close enough that two of them must end up in the same cubby; several pots are equally close to that shared spot, so no single pairing is singled out.

pigeonhole.name: tea_cup_sugar
pigeonhole.prompt_body: An Edo-period woodblock print in muted indigo, cream, and warm brown: on one low tea tray, show four small handleless cups, each already marked by a cube being lowered toward it, while a fifth sugar cube arrives with no free cup left. The extra cube must share one cup with another, but do not show which cup will get the pair; make several cups look equally close to taking two cubes. Keep the scene natural, everyday, and free of labels or diagram-like marks.

diagonalization.name: apartment_lights
diagonalization.prompt_body: On a straight-on nighttime apartment facade, make the windows read as a strict grid of rows and columns. Across the grid, a single diagonal of windows must stand out: in each row, exactly one window on that diagonal is flipped from the others in that row, switching lit to dark or closed curtain to open. Beside the building, add one extra horizontal strip of windows that matches row k everywhere except at position k, where it flips.

diagonalization.name: salt_evaporation_pans
diagonalization.prompt_body: Arrange a clear grid of everyday tea cups on market shelves, with rows and columns easy to see. Make one diagonal path of cups cross the whole grid, and at every diagonal position that cup must visibly flip from the rest of its row: dark where the row is light, open where the row is closed, so each row has exactly one mismatch in a different column. Just outside the grid, place one extra row whose k-th cup is the opposite of row k’s k-th cup, so it matches no row.

diagonalization.name: greenhouse_seed_trays
diagonalization.prompt_body: Show a kitchen potting bench as a clear 6x6 grid of small seedling pots. In each row, exactly one pot is visibly the opposite state from the others, and that flipped pot shifts one step to the right on every lower row so the opposite pots run from top-left to bottom-right. Beneath the grid, add one extra row that copies a chosen row everywhere except at the matching position, where it flips state.

diagonalization.name: harbor_slips
diagonalization.prompt_body: A crisp drone view of a marina laid out as a clean grid of boat slips, with rows as candidate lines and columns as features. Make one diagonal line of slips run across the grid; at every diagonal slip, the local state is visibly the opposite of the rest of its row, such as a white dinghy in an otherwise empty dark-water row or an empty slip in an otherwise filled row. Just outside the grid, add one extra row of slips that matches the columns but differs from row k in exactly the k-th position.

diagonalization.name: monastery_candles
diagonalization.prompt_body: A classical oil painting of a stone monastery candle wall, viewed squarely. Each drawn cell is one shallow niche in the drawn rows and columns, holding either a burning candle or a bare cold holder. The diagonal niches have small brass drip plates. On a low shelf below, an added row of holders has one per column, each opposite to the flame state of the matching diagonal niche.

diagonalization.name: parking_bays
diagonalization.prompt_body: Show a parking lot as a clean table-like grid of bays, with rows easy to count and each row using the same base pattern. A single diagonal chain of bays must run across the grid from upper left to lower right; in every bay on that line, the parked/not-parked state is visibly opposite to the rest of its row, so the changed bay shifts one position right on each lower row. Add one separate curbside row outside the main grid that copies a row pattern but flips the matching bay at that same position.

diagonalization.name: bamboo_fish_racks
diagonalization.prompt_body: Show a neat table-like grid of bamboo drying trays in a fishing village courtyard: each row is one candidate, each column is one position. A single path must step one cell farther right in every lower row, and every tray on that path must be visibly flipped from its row mate (fish to empty, or empty to fish). Outside the table, include one extra row that matches row 1, row 2, etc., except at position k where that one tray flips.

diagonalization.name: stained_glass_panes
diagonalization.prompt_body: An art nouveau stained-glass window photographed in soft daylight. Each drawn cell is one square pane, placed in the drawn rows and columns, either amber glass or deep blue glass. The diagonal panes are bordered by thin silver solder. Beneath the main window, an added transom row has one pane per column, each taking the opposite color from the diagonal pane directly above. No letters or symbols.

diagonalization.name: bakery_pastry_case
diagonalization.prompt_body: Show a bakery case arranged as a strict 6-by-6 grid of pastries, with rows and columns clearly visible. Start each row in the same pastry style, then make one pastry in row 1, column 1, row 2, column 2, and so on down to row 6, column 6 visibly flipped to the opposite frosting or decoration while the rest of that row stays unchanged. Place one separate tray outside the grid whose pastries match the rows except each tray row differs at its matching position.

aperiodic_tiling.name: harbor_roof
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: Fill the entire frame edge to edge with a sunlit stone courtyard made only of two interlocking tile shapes: kites and rhombs. Arrange them in a Penrose-like layout where small five-point star clusters appear in scattered places, but there is no single center, no radial layout, and no repeating block or translation unit; if you shift the whole image, it should never line up exactly. Keep the surface ordinary, seamless, and continuous off all four edges.

aperiodic_tiling.name: quilt_bed
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: A tabletop covered edge to edge with a Penrose-like patchwork of only two tile shapes: wide mustard rhombs and narrow deep-green kite/dart pieces. Every seam must obey the same local matching rule, so the layout never settles into a repeating block, strip, or grid. Scatter small five-point star clusters in several places, but avoid any central star, ring, or mirrored arrangement. Keep the whole frame filled with no border, no empty corners, and no fixed spacing pattern.

aperiodic_tiling.name: herb_terrace
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: Cover the entire rooftop garden edge to edge with only two paving stones: broad pale rhombs and slimmer dark kite-shaped stones, fitted by one local matching rule so the same joins keep reappearing everywhere without any repeating block or fixed-offset copy. Add scattered five-point star groupings as part of the paving, not as decoration. Keep it as a dusk herb garden with thyme, mint, and planters along the tile edges; no central fountain, no radial layout, no empty borders.

aperiodic_tiling.name: rain_courtyard
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: The temple courtyard floor must cover the entire frame edge to edge with only two interlocking paving stones: a broad tan diamond and a slimmer blue-black diamond. Lay them so the pattern has no shift that ever makes the whole floor line up again, and no identical block returns at a fixed spacing. Small five-point star clusters can appear here and there, but there must be no single center, no axis, and no repeating patch. Keep the wet stone, lanterns, and gate posts at the edges.

aperiodic_tiling.name: lantern_square
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: Cover the whole frame edge to edge with a floor made from only two interlocking stone shapes, tan kite-darts and charcoal rhombs, arranged so every local match rule is obeyed but no straight row, repeating block, or single center ever appears. Small five-point star clusters may pop up in scattered places, and any local patch should show up again at irregular distances without lining up into a fixed grid. Set this in a busy evening market with lanterns, stalls, and cropped passersby at the borders.

aperiodic_tiling.name: station_concourse
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: Lay the station concourse floor edge to edge with only two tile shapes: broad warm-gray rhombs and narrow charcoal kites, fitted exactly like the reference. Scatter small five-point star clusters in several places, but keep the field centerless, with no radial hub and no repeated block or sliding copy anywhere. Let the same local fitting rule continue across the full frame, so small patches reappear in different places while the floor never settles into a repeat.

aperiodic_tiling.name: salt_flats
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: Fill the entire frame edge to edge with a dry salt-pan landscape built from only two interlocking tile shapes, kite plates and dart plates, using one exact edge-matching rule everywhere. The same small five-point star clusters must appear in many places, and every local pattern should recur within a bounded distance, but never as a repeated block or by sliding the whole image. Keep a pale noon scene with thin water in the cracks, no border, no central hub, no spokes, no labels.

aperiodic_tiling.name: sewing_table
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: Use the exact Penrose-style arrangement of tan burlap rhombs and indigo kite-dart pieces across a sewing table, filling the entire frame edge to edge. The pieces must fit together in the same local layout everywhere, with small five-point star groupings scattered through the cloth, but no single center, no radial spread, and no repeated block. Keep it as an everyday craft scene with scissors, pins, thread, and scraps nearby.

aperiodic_tiling.name: greenhouse_walk
aperiodic_tiling.prompt_body: An overhead greenhouse floor fills the entire frame edge to edge with only two tile shapes, a broad diamond and a narrow dart, arranged by the same local join rules everywhere. The tiles must never line up into any repeating shift or regular grid; nearby clusters may echo each other, but no block can recur at a fixed interval. Scatter small five-point star-like clusters across the walkway, with plants and glass beams around the edges, and no central focal point or ring layout.

projective_duality.name: reef_polyps
projective_duality.prompt_body: A split underwater photograph of the SAME coral flat. LEFT: pale coral ridges are thick bright paths, matching every drawn stroke, while each drawn dot is a tiny closed sea-anemone polyp at the exact meeting place. RIGHT: at night, fluorescent polyps swell into bright beads at those same places, while the coral ridges shrink to thin blue seams. No labels, no arrows, no added branches.

projective_duality.name: canal_lanterns
projective_duality.prompt_body: Two-panel aerial view of the same desert farm, with the layout itself as the main structure: one panel shows large irrigation basins at every junction and the connecting canals as thin dark threads; the other panel keeps every bend, crossing, and spacing exactly the same, but the basins and canals trade places, so the basins become the narrow links and the channels become the broad shapes. Swap them a second time and the original arrangement returns exactly. No text, labels, or map style.

projective_duality.name: stained_glass_lead
projective_duality.prompt_body: Classical oil painting of two adjacent views of the SAME chapel window. LEFT: heavy black lead cames carry every drawn stroke, with tiny colored glass bosses marking each drawn dot. RIGHT: sunlight catches the bosses as large jeweled points, while the lead cames recede into hairline dark dividers. The placement, slants, and uneven distances match exactly between views; no inscriptions or heraldic marks.

projective_duality.name: tea_steam_bowls
projective_duality.prompt_body: A tidy afternoon tea on a wooden table in a side-by-side diptych: make the arrangement itself the skeleton. On the left, teacups are the holders and saucers are the bases; on the right, every cup and saucer take each other’s place everywhere at once, while the exact counts, spacing, pairings, and positions stay unchanged. Repeating the exchange would restore the first panel exactly. No text, labels, symbols, or viewpoint change.

projective_duality.name: forge_rivets
projective_duality.prompt_body: Industrial macro photograph diptych of the SAME iron gate corner. LEFT: black forged bars are thick strokes matching all drawn strokes, and each drawn dot is a low rivet head where bars meet. RIGHT: after polishing, rivet heads gleam as dominant metal points, while the bars are thin dark silhouettes between them. The same crossings, offsets, and unequal bar lengths must align precisely; no stamped letters or maker marks.

projective_duality.name: candle_wax_pools
projective_duality.prompt_body: Baroque still-life diptych of the SAME tabletop after a candlelit dinner. LEFT: streams of hardened wax form raised ivory strokes matching every drawn stroke, and each drawn dot is a small blackened wick fragment. RIGHT: candle flames relit at the wick fragments become bright points, while the wax streams turn into thin pale connectors. The same skewed quadrangle and all junctions remain unchanged; no books, notes, or labels.

projective_duality.name: salt_ponds
projective_duality.prompt_body: Modern aerial color view of a coastal salt farm split into left and right views. The four corner pump sheds are the drawn corners, and the straight dikes joining them are the drawn sides. On the left, the sheds are the heavy dark masses and the sluice mouths are tiny pale dots; on the right, the sluice mouths become the heavy bright masses and the sheds shrink to faint markers, while every relation between them stays in place.

projective_duality.name: joinery_bench
projective_duality.prompt_body: Macro photograph of a cabinetmaker's bench in warm workshop light. The four corner pegs on the clamp frame are the drawn corners, and the taut straps between them are the drawn sides. In the first view, the pegs read as solid brass heads and the straps as thin leather lines; in the second, the leather tabs swell into the main shapes and the pegs recede to small fastening points, yet each joint keeps the same partner.

projective_duality.name: harbor_cranes
projective_duality.prompt_body: Make the harbor scene itself carry the rule: use only two visible element types, thick dock posts and thin mooring ropes. In the left half, the posts are the anchors and the ropes only connect them; in the right half, the same harbor arrangement is shown again with those jobs exchanged, so ropes act as the anchors and posts become the connectors, while each boat stays attached to the same neighbor. Then show the original arrangement once more so the first reading is restored exactly. Keep it like a natural blue-hour quay, with no text or diagram look.

contraction_fixed_point.name: acetate_fern
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: A macro photograph of translucent acetate sheets on a light table: the first sheet holds a pressed fern silhouette, each later sheet shows that fern reduced to three fifths and shifted by the same down-right move. The rising guide becomes the table’s bright front seam, the bowed guide becomes a curved cut edge of acetate. Every sideways leg is a sheet edge, every upright leg another sheet edge, all ending at one unchanged pinhole.

contraction_fixed_point.name: salt_pan_channels
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: Aerial drone view of pale desert salt pans after rain, copper and white palette. The rising guide is a dry levee running from lower left to upper right; the bowed guide is a dark tidal creek. Each sideways segment becomes a straight salt road, each upright segment a narrow sluice gate, the next pair always two thirds as long as the last. The single chain tightens toward the levee-creek crossing, where a still black pool remains.

contraction_fixed_point.name: chapel_carpets
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: A late Renaissance oil painting inside a quiet stone chapel, warm umber and candle gold. The rising guide becomes a slanting marble aisle seam; the bowed guide becomes the curved altar rail. Every horizontal stroke is a red carpet edge laid across the aisle, every vertical stroke is its forward fold, each fold shorter by a constant share. The final tiny carpet corner rests exactly where seam and rail meet, with no inscription anywhere.

contraction_fixed_point.name: raked_sand_pebble
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: A monochrome ink drawing of a small courtyard of raked sand viewed from above. The rising guide becomes a dark rake furrow drawn across the sand; the bowed guide becomes the wet edge around a shallow puddle. Every sideways mark is a crisp rake pass, every upright mark is a short row of fallen pebbles, each new pass-and-pebble pair reduced to half the last. All marks settle on one black pebble at the furrow-puddle contact.

contraction_fixed_point.name: bowl_marble_trace
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: Show one continuous glowing path that turns toward a single still point, with at least five visible straight segments. Each new segment should be about half the length of the one before it, so the path clearly gets shorter step by step until the last pieces pile up at the same spot. Use a realistic tabletop scene: a steel marble tracing the path inside a matte black bowl under one blue-white lamp, with the final bright dot fixed where the path ends.

contraction_fixed_point.name: quarry_haul_roads
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: In an overhead satellite-style view of a small limestone quarry yard, show one single service path built by repeating the same turn on the end of the previous segment: each new straight section is about half as long as the last, for at least five steps, all along one route and tightening into one fixed stopping point beside a pale seam. Mark that point with a parked loader, and make the final short segments visibly pile up there as the path stops.

contraction_fixed_point.name: glass_leadwork
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: Show one continuous stained-glass lead path in a garden-window scene stepping inward toward one small fixed bead: a wide strip begins at the frame, then folds to a shorter segment, then shorter again, with each new segment about half the previous length, for at least five visible steps. The segments must all belong to the same path and pile up at the same tiny stationary point, marked by a still glass jewel where the path ends. Use amber, teal, and smoky violet; no labels or diagram look.

contraction_fixed_point.name: curtain_shadow_steps
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: One visible path must fold toward a single resting point across the scene: start from a curtain cord shadow on a wooden floor and make it step forward in at least five clear bent segments, each segment about half the length of the previous one, all on the same line of travel, until the shadows pile up at one tiny dust mote that stays fixed and the last segment stops there. Keep the setting as a quiet morning window with a linen curtain, floorboards, and soft light.

contraction_fixed_point.name: tile_stairwell
contraction_fixed_point.prompt_body: Long-exposure photograph of an old tiled stairwell landing in cool gray and brass tones. A single curved grout seam is the rule, a straight wall seam beside it is the return line, and a lone glass marble traces a chain of shorter right-angle hops between them. Each hop lands closer to the same pale corner tile at the base of the stairs, where the marble finally comes to rest unchanged.
